newsitem.title: EGYPT: Arab world's poet speaks on Palestinian violence.
newsitem.headline: Arab world's poet speaks on Palestinian violence.

text.p: Angered by Israel and the United States, the Arab world's most prominent living poet announced on Friday: "how fine is terrorism."

In a poem by that title, launched on the front page of the international newspaper al-Hayat, Nizar Qabbani of Syria echoed increasing Arab frustration at the way Israeli and American politicians deny Palestinians the right to resist occupation.
Qabbani's political poems are part of the discourse between intellectuals across the Arab world. Sometimes they spark off controversies which rumble on for months.

"We are accused of terrorism..." begins his latest offering, written in London on April 15 and drawing on the deadlock in Middle East peace talks since Israeli bulldozers started work on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
Then how fine is terrorism," the poem says.
If we refuse to be wiped out
At the hands of the Mongols, the Jews and barbarians,
At the window of the Security Council which
The Caesar of Caesars has taken over," it adds.
The newspaper published the first 22 stanzas of the poem and said more would follow.
